exposure: Pregnant patients who underwent rIVCF placement without adjunct catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT)
Elective cesarean section vs. other delivery mode
Retrievable inferior vena cava filter (rIVCF) placement during pregnancy or postpartum
Pregnant patients who underwent rIVCF placement with adjunct CDT
Postpartum patients who underwent rIVCF placement
Timing of rIVCF placement (during pregnancy vs. postpartum)
cohort: 24 women who underwent rIVCF placement during pregnancy/postpartum between 2005-2016 at a single center (also included pooled analysis of 98 patients from the literature)
finding: Frequent rIVCF-related complications, radiation exposure, and removal failure warrant cautious utilization of rIVCFs in obstetric patients, and the benefit of suprarenal placement and elective cesarean section remains unclear.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean section did not significantly reduce overall complication and retrieval rates (p = .19).
